I am sixty-five years old. I have worked this land for forty years, and I never went to school, but the fields have taught me everything I need. My farm is fifteen mu, and it is just my husband and me at home now—our children work in the factories in the city. We have a good well, so I do not worry about water.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October. I have twelve mu of wheat, planted with the improved seed I get from the county supply shop. It grows well here. This spring, when the wheat turns green, I will spread urea by hand and run the rotary tiller between the rows. I will irrigate three times from the well—once when it greens up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray twice for insects and once for weeds. I do not change what works. I expect about five hundred kilograms per mu if the weather holds.

I keep three mu for garlic. Garlic is my cash crop—it brings more money than grain. I plant my own cloves that I saved from last year’s harvest; they are clean and sprout well. Garlic needs more food and water than wheat. I spread compound fertilizer and urea, and I irrigate three times because garlic must not dry out. I also spray three times for weeds and diseases. I till that plot with the rotary tiller too. Last year I got about fifteen hundred kilograms per mu, and I will do the same this year.

After the wheat and garlic are harvested in early summer, I plant maize on all fifteen mu. For maize, you must use hybrid seed from the shop—if you plant your own saved seed, the yield drops by half. I broadcast compound fertilizer as basal dressing and plant right after harvest without much tillage; there is no time to waste between crops. Maize needs two irrigations in summer, and I spray twice for weeds and insects. I expect about six hundred kilograms per mu.

I am getting old, and my back is not what it used to be. My husband helps when he is not working odd jobs in the village. I keep my methods simple and stick to what I know. I do not waste money on fancy inputs, and I do not take risks.
